courses.title: Introduction to Architectural Design Theories and Methods
courses.description: This foundational, First-Year Experience course introduces students to “design thinking,” exploring the built environment through lectures, readings, and activities that address different design approaches. Includes studies of historical precedents; an exposition of various design philosophies; and an introduction to the tools, techniques, and methods relevant in the design process.

courses.title: Visual Literacy and Civilization: An Architect’s View
courses.description: [GE 3B] The role of visual explanation in Western European civilization, while also emphasizing its cultural relativity. Analysis of the rules of representational conventions in the context of their rich cultural history, and contrasts them with non-western traditions. Introduction to several of 20th century’s schools of thought that have been critical of the hegemonic visual regime of modernity, and its role in colonial expansion and domination of non-western cultures. Corequisite(s): ARC 1022A .

courses.title: Visual Literacy and Civilization: An Architect’s View Activity
courses.description: [GE 3B] Focus on the role of visual explanation in the history of Western European world. Opportunities to discuss the readings introduced in ARC 1020, and to conduct drawing exercises that will illustrate these reading. Corequisite(s): ARC 1020 .

courses.title: World Architecture before the Renaissance
courses.description: [GE 3A] Survey of architecture of ancient Near East, Egypt, Greece and Rome, early Christian and Byzantine eras and Romanesque and Gothic periods in Western Europe. Introduction to major non-western architectural traditions. Corequisite(s): ARC 3612 .
courses.prerequisites: GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: World Architecture before the Renaissance Discussion
courses.description: [GE 3A] Survey of the architecture of ancient Near East, Egypt, Greece and Rome, early Christian and Byzantine eras and Romanesque and Gothic periods in Western Europe, and introduces major non-western architectural traditions. Opportunity for small group discussions and student presentations dealing with above themes in greater detail and depth. Corequisite(s): ARC 3610 .
courses.prerequisites: GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: World Art: Prehistory through Medieval Europe
courses.description: [GE 3A] Comprehensive survey and analysis of the development of art in ancient civilizations from prehistoric times through the Middle Ages (ca. 30,000 BCE through 14th century).
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Interpreting Architecture
courses.description: [GE 3C] Dual Listed as: ARC 5630 Interprets architecture as a physical embodiment of civilization. Discusses architecture in the context of parallel developments in art, philosophy, literature, science, and technology. Analyzes various cultural, social, and economic factors that shape the built environment.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Advocacy and Argument
courses.description: [GE 1C] Study and practice of the principles and skills of effective oral argument, including how to conceptualize, structure, support, and deliver oral arguments. Focuses on how to create reasoned oral arguments, adapt arguments to different audiences, and critique the arguments of others.

courses.title: Written Reasoning
courses.description: [GE 1B] Inquiry into written reasoning in actual rhetorical situations. Analysis of relations among logical claims, lines of reasoning, interpretation of evidence, and the judgment of these by audiences. Papers and critical reading of non-fiction argumentation.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Trigonometry
courses.description: [GE 2] Right triangle trigonometry, the unit circle, trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions, trigonometric identities, equations, graphs, Law of Sines and Law of Cosines, applications of trigonometry, complex numbers and DeMoivre’s Formula. Applications of trigonometry to solve problems.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Physics of Motion, Fluids, and Heat
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to Newtonian mechanics and thermodynamics: Kinematics, forces, conservation laws, viscous fluids, heat transfer, and the microscopic nature of gases. Emphasis on biological applications. Corequisite(s): PHY 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 106, MAT 1060 , MAT 112, MAT 114, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 115, MAT 116, MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , or MAT 1300 . ( MAT 1300 can be concurrent.)

courses.title: Physics of Motion, Fluids, and Heat Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Experiments on Newtonian mechanics, fluids, and heat. Corequisite(s): PHY 1210 .

courses.title: Foundation Design 1 Activity
courses.description: An introduction to the process of design through studio projects addressing the role of process in the development of form. Focus on drawing and model construction as a means to seeing and understanding. Corequisite(s): ARC 1011 and ARC 1501A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Undergraduate Standing.

courses.title: Foundation Design 2 Activity
courses.description: Continuing exploration of the design process and the formal and spatial language of architecture. Use of architectural case studies, and two and three-dimensional communication technique. Corequisite(s): ARC 1021 and ARC 1502A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 1010 , ARC 1011A , ARC 1011 , and ARC 1501A .

courses.title: Second Year Design 1 Activity
courses.description: The design process using simple programs and the influence of context. Introduction to environmental and structural constraints in architectural design. Corequisite(s): ARC 2011 and ARC 2501A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing and C or better in ARC 1021A , ARC 1021 , and ARC 1502A .

courses.title: Second Year Design 2 Activity
courses.description: A continuation of basic design exercises focusing on simple buildings and their relationship to site and program. Introduction to environmental and structural constraints in architectural design. Corequisite(s): ARC 2021 and ARC 2502A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Undergraduate Standing, ARC 2011 , ARC 2011A , and ARC 2501A .

courses.title: Third Year Design 1 Activity
courses.description: The design process as it relates to building materials and construction. The interaction of aesthetic, technological, and economic determinants. Introduction to building codes. *A special section of ARC 2990L will be assigned to students who do not pass the portfolio review. Passing this class with a C or better will satisfy the portfolio requirement. Corequisite(s): ARC 3010A , ARC 3011 , ARC 3220 , and ARC 3222 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 2021A , ARC 2021 , and ARC 2502A .

courses.title: Third Year Design 2 Activity
courses.description: Interaction of construction technology, human behavior, site development in the design of multi-family housing in a specific context. Introduction to urban issues. Corequisite(s): ARC 3021 , ARC 3420 , ARC 3422 , ARC 4400 , and ARC 4402A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Undergraduate Standing, ARC 3011A , ARC 3011 , and ARC 3010A .

courses.title: Topics in Architectural Design 1 Activity
courses.description: Topics in Advanced Architectural Design. See department of architecture office and/or website for list of topics offered. Corequisite(s): ARC 4011 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3021A , ARC 3021 , and ARC 3020A .

courses.description: Topics in Advanced Architectural Design. See department of architecture office and/or website for list of topics offered.

courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 4021A , ARC 4021 , and ARC 4502A .

courses.title: Senior Project Design Activity
courses.description: Preparation of an architectural project design proposal for the bachelor’s degree project. See department of architecture office and/or website for list of tracks offered. Corequisite(s): ARC 4620 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 4031A , ARC 4031 , ARC 4503A , and ARC 4610.

courses.title: Foundation Design 1 Lecture
courses.description: An introduction to the process of design addressing the role of process in the development of form. Lecture discussion. Corequisite(s): ARC 1011A and ARC 1501A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Undergraduate Standing.

courses.title: Architectural Programming
courses.description: Study of the role that architectural programming plays in the design of buildings. Architect’s responsibility to respond to the physical, social and regulatory conditions of the building site and context. Corequisite(s): ARC 2011A and ARC 2501A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 1021A , ARC 1021 , and ARC 1502A .

courses.title: Introduction to Sustainable Architectural Design
courses.description: Basic principles for the design of sustainable environments at the urban, site and building scale. Emphasis on site design and the design of sustainable buildings and their connection to a specific context. Corequisite(s): ARC 2021A and ARC 2502A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 2011A , and ARC 2011 .

courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 4021A , and ARC 4021 . ARC 4021 - Topics in Architectural Design 2 (1)

courses.title: Senior Project Material and Structural Integration
courses.description: Integrating senior project design with structural and nonstructural systems, materials and codes. Perform structural, code and material analyses for their individual senior project designs based on their developed designs and information from ARC 4610. Corequisite(s): ARC 4611A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing and ARC 4610.

courses.title: Foundation Digital Design 1 Activity
courses.description: Digital design drawing and modeling, tools, skills and concepts actively used in the concurrent design studio. Corequisite(s): ARC 1011A and ARC 1011 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing.

courses.title: Foundation Digital Design 2 Activity
courses.description: Digital design drawing and modeling, tools, skills and concepts actively used in the concurrent design studio. Corequisite(s): ARC 1021A and ARC 1021 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing and ARC 1501A .

courses.title: Intermediate Digital Design 1 Activity
courses.description: Facilitates student access to digital design drawing and modeling, tools, skills and concepts actively used in the design studio. Use of sketching and digital modeling for design study, iteration and variation. Corequisite(s): ARC 2011A and ARC 2011 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 1502A , ARC 1021 , and ARC 1021A .

courses.title: Intermediate Digital Design 2 Activity
courses.description: Facilitates student access to digital design drawing and modeling, tools, skills and concepts actively used in the design studio. Use of sketching and digital modeling for design study, iteration and variation. Corequisite(s): ARC 2021A and ARC 2021 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing and ARC 2501A .

courses.title: Architectural Codes
courses.description: Study of relevant codes for architects for the protection of the health, safety and welfare of the public as they relate to architectural design. Corequisite(s): ARC 3011 , ARC 3011A , ARC 3220 , and ARC 3222 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 2021A , ARC 2021 , and ARC 2502A .

courses.title: Housing and Urban Design Activity
courses.description: Interaction of building technology, human behavior, and site development in the design of mixed-use multi-family housing projects. Exploration of urban design issues including research and analysis of topics associated with mixed use projects. Corequisite(s): ARC 3021 and ARC 3021A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing and ARC 3010A .

courses.title: Structures 1
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5210 The relationship of structure to form, function and economics. Analysis of structural systems, including the determination of forces and stresses. Introduction to the geometric properties of structural members, and designing trusses. Corequisite(s): ARC 3212 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 2011A , ARC 2011 , ARC 2501A , PHY 1210 , and PHY 1210L .

courses.title: Structures 1 Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5212 The relationship of structure to form, function and economics. Analysis of structural systems, including the determination of forces and stresses. Introduction to the geometric properties of structural members, and designing trusses. Corequisite(s): ARC 3210 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 2011A , ARC 2011 , ARC 2501A , PHY 1210 , and PHY 1210L .

courses.title: Structures 2
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5220 The relationship of structure to form, function, and economics. Analysis of structural systems, including designing structural members in steel, concrete and masonry. Design of seismic and wind resisting structural systems. Corequisite(s): ARC 3011 , ARC 3011A , and ARC 3222 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3210 , and ARC 3212 .

courses.title: Structures 2 Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5222 The relationship of structure to form, function, and economics. Analysis of structural systems, including designing structural members in steel, concrete and masonry. Design of seismic and wind resisting structural systems. Dicussion. Corequisite(s): ARC 3011 , ARC 3011A , and ARC 3220 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3210 , and ARC 3212 .

courses.title: Environmental Controls Systems 1
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5310 Performance principles and systems to reduce the environmental impact of buildings and to address occupant comfort. Thermal comfort, climate analysis, solar geometry, daylighting, passive heating and cooling, renewable energy and mechanical systems. Corequisite(s): ARC 3312 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 1021A , ARC 1021 , and ARC 1502A .

courses.title: Environmental Controls Systems 1 Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5312 Performance principles and systems to reduce the environmental impact of buildings and to address occupant comfort. Thermal comfort, climate analysis, solar geometry, daylighting, passive heating and cooling, renewable energy and mechanical systems. Corequisite(s): ARC 3310 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 1021A , ARC 1021 , and ARC 1502A .

courses.title: Environmental Controls 2
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5320 Performance principles and systems to safeguard occupant comfort while reducing environmental impact and approaching carbon neutrality. Survey of lighting, HVAC systems, acoustics, plumbing, electric and other building control systems. Corequisite(s): ARC 3322 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3310 , and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Environmental Controls 2 Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5322 Performance principles and systems to safeguard occupant comfort while reducing environmental impact and approaching carbon neutrality. Survey of lighting, HVAC systems, acoustics, plumbing, electric and other building control systems. Corequisite(s): ARC 3320 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3310 , and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Building Construction 1
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5440 Techniques of construction, building components, and building systems. Includes introduction to construction materials (wood, steel, concrete & masonry) for structural and nonstructural applications, construction techniques and specification systems. Introduction to architectural construction drawing documentation. Corequisite(s): ARC 3412 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 1021A , ARC 1021 , and ARC 1502A .

courses.title: Building Construction 1 Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5442 Techniques of construction, building components, and building systems. Includes introduction to construction materials (wood, steel, concrete & masonry) for structural and nonstructural applications, construction techniques and specification systems. Introduction to architectural construction drawing documentation. Corequisite(s): ARC 3410 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 1021A , ARC 1021 , and ARC 1502A .

courses.title: Building Construction 2
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5450 Techniques of construction, building components, and systems investigated through case studies. Further exploration of properties of materials used in construction and their specification both in written and drawing formats. Emphasis on systems design for structure, weatherproofing and sustainable design with respect to materials selection/interaction. Corequisite(s): ARC 3021 , ARC 3021A , and ARC 3422 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3410 , and ARC 3412 .

courses.title: Building Construction 2 Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5452 Techniques of construction, building components, and systems investigated through case studies. Further exploration of properties of materials used in construction and their specification both in written and drawing formats. Emphasis on systems design for structure, weatherproofing and sustainable design with respect to materials selection/interaction. Corequisite(s): ARC 3021 , ARC 3021A , and ARC 3420 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3410 , and ARC 3412 .

courses.title: Architecture from Renaissance through Modern Era
courses.description: Cultural, social and aesthetic forces that shaped architecture and urban design during the Renaissance and Baroque periods, and from the Eighteenth, through Twentieth Centuries. Particular attention to the emergence of the Modern movement. Corequisite(s): ARC 3622 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3610 , and ARC 3612 .

courses.title: Architecture from Renaissance through Modern Era Discussion
courses.description: Cultural, social and aesthetic forces that shaped architecture and urban design during the Renaissance and Baroque periods, and from the Eighteenth, through Twentieth Centuries. Particular attention to the emergence of the Modern movement. Corequisite(s): ARC 3620 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3610 , and ARC 3612 .

courses.title: Design Development
courses.description: An overview of construction, building components, and systems investigated through case studies. Study of the connection between material properties, fabrication techniques, and building design. Corequisite(s): ARC 3021 , ARC 3021A , and ARC 4402A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3011A , ARC 3011 , ARC 3220 , and ARC 3222 .

courses.title: Design Development Activity
courses.description: An overview of construction, building components, and systems investigated through case studies. Study of the connection between material properties, fabrication techniques, and building design. Corequisite(s): ARC 3021 , ARC 3021A , and ARC 4400 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3011A , ARC 3011 , ARC 3220 , and ARC 3222 .

courses.title: Advanced Digital Design 1 Activity
courses.description: Facilitates student access to digital design drawing and modeling, tools, skills and concepts actively used in design studio. Assignments support design studio discussion with an emphasis on advanced Building Information Modeling (BIM).
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3021A , ARC 3021 , and ARC 3020A.

courses.title: Advanced Digital Design 2 Activity
courses.description: Facilitates student access to digital design drawing and modeling, tools, skills and concepts actively used in design studio. Assignments support design studio discussion with an emphasis on advanced Building Information Modeling (BIM).
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing and ARC 4501A .

courses.title: Advanced Digital Design 3 Activity
courses.description: Facilitates student access to digital design drawing and modeling, tools, skills and concepts actively used in design studio. Assignments support design studio discussion with an emphasis on advanced Building Information Modeling (BIM).
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing and ARC 4502A .

courses.title: Senior Project Research and Programming
courses.description: Site selection and analysis, and the development of a building program in support of a student’s senior project. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, junior or senior standing, ARC 4021A , ARC 4021 , and ARC 4502A .

courses.title: Architectural Practice
courses.description: The administrative, legal, ethical aspects of the architectural profession and the relationship between the profession and the construction industry. Corequisite(s): ARC 4712 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3021A , ARC 3021 , ARC 4400 , and ARC 4402A .

courses.title: Architectural Practice Discussion
courses.description: The administrative, legal, ethical aspects of the architectural profession and the relationship between the profession and the construction industry. Corequisite(s): ARC 4710 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3021A , ARC 3021 , ARC 4400 , and ARC 4402A .

courses.title: The Architect and the Development Process
courses.description: The potential roles of the architect in the development process are discussed. Issues include goals, appraisal of needs, economics, and market analysis feasibility studies, appraisal procedures, cash flow methods, financing options, decisions, design and delivery processes, involvement at levels of design decisions and project administration. Corequisite(s): ARC 4732 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing and ARC 3212 .

courses.title: The Architect and the Development Process Discussion
courses.description: The potential roles of the architect in the development process are discussed. Issues include goals, appraisal of needs, economics, and market analysis feasibility studies, appraisal procedures, cash flow methods, financing options, decisions, design and delivery processes, involvement at levels of design decisions and project administration. Corequisite(s): ARC 4730 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, ARC 3021 , and ARC 3021A .

courses.title: Drawing as Theory
courses.description: Exploration of the theory and history of architectural representation. Corequisite(s): ARC 4162A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, junior standing, or senior standing.

courses.title: Drawing as Theory Activity
courses.description: Introduction to the theory and history of architectural representation through hands-on drawing instruction and expanded discussion of assigned readings. Corequisite(s): ARC 4160 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, junior standing, or senior standing.

courses.title: Advanced Urban Design
courses.description: Design research and case-study analysis of urban theories, patterns, and form. Short design project.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing, Junior Standing, or Senior Standing.

courses.title: Architecture and Urbanism
courses.description: Examination of urban theories that form the basis for the design of buildings in modern urban and suburban settings.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, junior standing, or senior standing.

courses.title: Urbanism and Film
courses.description: Survey of Los Angeles’ portrayal in film and how portrayal has affected the view of the city’s neighborhoods, their people and landscapes. Discussions on growth, infrastructure, transportation, demography, and history in relation to issues of race, class, violence, youth, fame and fortune.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing, Junior Standing, or Senior Standing.

courses.title: Advanced Structural Design
courses.description: Topics of importance centered on structural design. Emphasis is on the exploration of space, structure and performance. Utilization of geometrically complex configurations to analyze the relationship between architectural and structural design.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing, Junior Standing, or Senior Standing; ARC 4250 or Instructor Permission.

courses.title: Sustainable Technology
courses.description: Integration and management of buildings systems to minimize environmental impact and reduce a building’s environmental footprint. Topics include sustainable materials, green building design criteria, passive heating and cooling systems, active solar systems, sustainable building and energy technologies, green building rating systems. Seminar-discussion course with emphasis on student research.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3310 ; and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Tools for Sustainability
courses.description: Environmental assessment tools for sustainable design. Computational tools for the early stages of design to evaluate and estimate building performance.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3310 ; and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Advanced Architectural Lighting
courses.description: Performance analysis and design application using computer simulation and laboratory testing of luminous environment in architecture to achieve visual comfort and special lighting effects.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3310 ; and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Carbon Neutral Architectural Design
courses.description: Concepts, strategies and tools for the design of low carbon, resilient buildings. Emphasis is on design factors that affect building impact on climate. Special emphasis is on emissions embodied in materials and energy use. Implementation and development of tools and strategies to design resilient, low carbon buildings that will help to reduce anthropogenic emissions.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3310 ; and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Advanced Architectural Materials Research
courses.description: Advanced research connecting material properties, fabrication techniques, and building design.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3420 ; and ARC 3422 .

courses.title: Digitally Enhanced Construction and Fabrication Activity
courses.description: Survey and in-depth case studies of how to manufacture, produce and build non-standard current architectural projects. Class discussions centered on issues related to traditional versus contemporary building and documentation methods. Emphasis on advanced CAD/BIM modeling and direct output to manufacturers.Hybrid Asynchronous course.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; and ARC 2501A , ARC 3420 , or ARC 5510A .

courses.title: American Architecture
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5640 Development of American buildings and infrastructure in response to changes in material and methods of construction, demography and cultural values contributing to evolving built environment. Includes history of American architectural profession. Corequisite(s): ARC 4642 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC senior or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: American Architecture Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 5642 Development of American buildings and infrastructure in response to changes in material and methods of construction, demography and cultural values contributing to evolving built environment. Includes history of American architectural profession. Corequisite(s): ARC 4640 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC senior or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: California Architecture
courses.description: Evolution of California’s built environment comprised of designed landscapes, architecture and infrastructure. Architectural developments in response to climate, landscape and the vision of design professionals. Ongoing contribution of California design to the present. Field trips.
courses.prerequisites: ARC senior or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: Managing a Design Firm
courses.description: The study of the relationship between the architect, employee, client, and contractor; including a study of new business development strategies, winning a commission, marketing, and client communications.
courses.prerequisites: ARC 4710 and ARC 4712 or Instructor Permission.

courses.title: Teaching Practicum
courses.description: Aids instructor in preparing course material, giving software and model-making tutorials to students, facilitating in-class discussions, and engaging in student mentoring.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: Archives Practicum Activity
courses.description: Introduction to standard archival practices, focus on the specific issues associated with the arrangement and storage of architectural records and investigate projects that incorporate archival materials. Work supports activities of the ENV Archives-Special Collections.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing, Advanced Standing, or Instructor Permission.

courses.title: Indigenous Architecture
courses.description: Survey and in-depth case studies of architectural forms produced by non literate and traditional societies around the world. Emphasis given to social, cultural and cosmological factors contributing to the variety of built forms, responses of form to climate and natural conditions, materials and methods of construction, and aesthetic expression.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: Topics in Preservation
courses.description: Discussion and research in specific areas of historic preservation including the history and documentation of historical resources, resources associated with under-represented groups and emerging research into the assessment of cultural resources. Includes a design exercise involving the documentation or adaptation of a historic building.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: Community Practicum Service Learning
courses.description: Community-Based Design Seminar in which students will engage applied research, analysis and design demonstrated by field studies and executed design recommendations and/or project implementation.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, senior standing, junior standing, or consent of instructor; and ARC 3021A .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to three times for a total credit of 9 units.

courses.title: Design Issues in Housing
courses.description: Behavioral, social and cultural issues in housing design as they relate to domestic organization, life cycle, class and ethnicity. Considerations of function and meaning in form-making, design adaptations in light of change, and evaluation procedures.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing or Advanced Standing; and Instructor Permission.

courses.title: Healthcare Architecture, Planning and Design
courses.description: Investigation of integrated planning, design, and construction process for healthcare architecture. New paradigm shift in healthcare policies and their social and economic impacts on innovative design of healing environments. Seminar engages students in research and analysis of healthcare design topics.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, senior standing, junior standing, or consent of instructor; and ARC 3021A .

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.
